prompt: The castle at sunset, seen from high above at a three-quarter angle: the sun sits low on the horizon in an orange and pink sky, warm orange light on one side of every wall and tower and long blue shadows across the grid on the other, the river glowing gold, the windows lit. Only this one castle stands in the land, no ruins and no other walls. Paint the near castle of the attached image, the one in the lower left with the square keep, the timber lookout under an orange pyramid roof and the red flag, as the only castle of a new picture, in the same soft painterly 2D look and colours. Keep its keep, roofs, walls and towers as they are in the attached image. Every cannon is a complete bronze barrel on one wooden carriage with two wheels, standing on the stone courtyard floor inside the walls, never on a wall, a wall walk, a tower, a roof or a house, its barrel raised to about 45 degrees. No cannon fires, no smoke from any gun. Rules for the whole picture: the land carries the painted tile grid in the same perspective as the buildings, its lines parallel to the castle walls. Castle walls are straight cream stone walls along the grid, with square or round corner towers, never curved walls. Keep the bottom right corner of the picture calm: it shows only grass, trees, ground or water. Not too busy, nothing too small, and the land is not bare. No people. No text, no letters, no numbers, no title, no watermark. Soft colours, not oversaturated, not a 3D render.
